chunks: It has been narrated from Al-Asbagh ibn Nubātah that he said:

One day, while we were around Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام in the Masjid of Kūfah, he said: “O people of Kūfah, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has bestowed upon you what He has not bestowed upon anyone else through the excellence of your place of prayer: the house of Ādam, the house of Nūḥ, the house of Idrīs, the place of prayer of Ibrāhīm al-Khalīl, the place of prayer of my brother al-Khiḍr عليه السلام, and my place of prayer.”

Indeed, this mosque of yours is surely one of the four mosques that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, chose for its people. It is as though I see it on the Day of Resurrection, having been brought wearing two white garments, resembling one in iḥrām; it will intercede for its people and for whoever prays in it, and its intercession will not be rejected. Days and nights will not pass until the Black Stone is set in it.

A time will surely come upon it when it will be the place of prayer of al-Mahdī from my descendants and the place of prayer of every believer. No believer will remain upon the earth except that he will either be there or his heart will yearn toward it. So do not forsake it, and seek nearness to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, through salat in it, and turn eagerly to Him in the fulfillment of your needs there. If people knew what blessing is in it, they would come to it from the farthest regions of the earth, even crawling upon snow.”

key_terms.الْبَرَكَةِ: blessing; the divine grace and goodness contained in the mosque
key_terms.الْحَجَرُ الْأَسْوَدُ: the Black Stone; mentioned here as being set in the mosque
key_terms.الْمَسَاجِدِ: mosques; the selected sanctuaries of worship
key_terms.الْمَهْدِيِّ: the Mahdi; the guided one from the Imam’s descendants
key_terms.شَفَاعَتُهُ: its intercession; the mosque’s accepted pleading for its people
key_terms.مُصَلَّاكُمْ: your place of prayer; the sacred worship-space being praised
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Resurrection; the time of final judgment

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about the virtue of Masjid al-Kūfah and its connection to al-Mahdī عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the unique sanctity and spiritual rank of Masjid al-Kūfah, linking it to earlier prophets and to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام. It portrays the mosque as a chosen place of worship and intercession on the Day of Resurrection, and it foretells its connection to al-Mahdī from the progeny of the Imam عليه السلام. The narration urges believers not to abandon it and to seek nearness to Allah through salat and supplication there.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.696 - It has been reported from Al-Asbagh ibn Nubata that He said:

One day while we were with Amir al-Mu'minin (as) in the Mosque of Kufa, Imam (as) said:
"O’ people of Kufa, Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, has blessed you with something no one else has been blessed with—the virtue of your place of prayer, which was the house of Adam, the house of Noah, the house of Idris, the place of prayer of Ibrahim (as) the Friend (Khalil), the place of prayer of my brother al-Khidr (as), and my place of prayer.

This mosque of yours is one of the four mosques chosen by Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, for its people.
I can see it on the Day of Judgment, coming in two white garments, resembling a pilgrim in ihram, and it will intercede for its people and for those who pray in it; its intercession will not be rejected. The days and nights will not pass until the Black Stone is placed in it.

A time will come when it will be the place of prayer for the Mahdi from my descendants and the place of prayer for every believer. No believer will remain on the earth without either being there or having their heart yearn toward it.
So, do not abandon it. Seek nearness to Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, by praying in it, and turn to Him to fulfil your needs in it.
If people knew the blessings it contains, they would come to it from all corners of the earth, even if they had to crawl on ice."
